clue.text: Popular protest given audible sign of approval

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: something audible is heard rather than seen, so the word for the sign is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tick is the mark of approval on schoolwork

explanation.surface: A popular protest wins a murmur of approval from onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audible' says that TICK is only heard, so it is spelt TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotic language or culture is that of ordinary people, so it is popular in the old sense.

clue.text: Retiring old man, one with bug

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: pater is old slang for father, the old man
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A retired father turns out to be a man with a bug, perhaps an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' turns PATERIW round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug a phone is to fit a listening device to it, which is a wiretap.

clue.text: I'll take minutes to cut into individual fruit

indicators.note: pieces that cut into something are placed inside it, here inside the word for an individual

parts.note: an individual is a person
the I of the contraction is taken as the letter I
M is the abbreviation for minute, doubled for the plural as pp is for pages

explanation.surface: Someone announces they will keep the minutes before slicing up a single piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is a link here: I takes MM, and the group IMM goes into PERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: A persimmon is an orange tropical fruit, also called a sharon fruit.

clue.text: He painted Scot without clothing? Rubbish

indicators.note: stripping the clothing removes the outer letters, leaving the middle of the word Scot

parts.note: rot is rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the idea that a famous artist painted a Scotsman in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without clothing' strips S and T off SCOT to leave CO. Corot was a 19th-century French landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot was the French painter of Barbizon landscapes, so he is one who painted.

clue.text: Fellow with constant bad back

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, as the speed of light in physics

indicators.note: back means the word for bad is read in reverse

parts.note: evil means bad

explanation.surface: A man has a persistent bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns EVIL into LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clive is a man's first name, and crosswords often use fellow to signal any such name.

clue.text: Attacked citadel on rocks

indicators.note: to be on the rocks is to be in ruins, so the letters break up and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fortress perched on rocks was assaulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' reads as part of 'on rocks' but is fodder: CITADEL plus ON make the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace into someone is an idiom for attacking them fiercely, physically or verbally.

clue.text: He gets worked up about endless paperwork for teachers

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the first phrase's letters wrap the paperwork

parts.note: taken as written
he stresses means he gets worked up and anxious

indicators.note: endless means losing the last letter of the word for paperwork

parts.note: admin is office paperwork

explanation.surface: A man gets anxious over the never-ending paperwork staff have to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets worked up' reads as describing the man, but it is the verb form: he stresses. 'endless' trims the last letter of the paperwork word.
explanation.definitionFit: Headmistresses are female head teachers, so they are teachers in charge of schools.

clue.text: Novel, say, cutting danger with weapons in reserve

indicators.note: cutting means splitting the word for danger open with the other piece inside

parts.note: a threat is a danger
e.g. means for example, as say does
gats is old American slang for guns
by as in put by or stand by means held in reserve

explanation.surface: Someone describes a threat being cut short by weapons kept back in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the usual crossword signal for 'for example'. The Great Gatsby is F. Scott Fitzgerald's 1925 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Gatsby is a famous American novel by F. Scott Fitzgerald.

clue.text: Part of letter?

definitions.meaning: a part in a play is a role, one person in the story
a letter of the alphabet is a written symbol of that kind

explanation.surface: It asks what makes up one portion of a written letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is both a role in a play and a written symbol such as a letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: Briefly think about artist's painting

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for think is wrapped round the artist
briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: to mull something over is to think about it
RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to think for a moment about an artist's picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'think about' looks like one phrase, but 'about' is the container signal; RA (Royal Academician) is the standard crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A mural is a painting done directly on a wall.

clue.text: Drive empty limousine, parking near motorway turning

indicators.note: turning means the whole run of pieces is turned round and read backwards
emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: An instruction to drive an empty limousine, parking it close to a motorway junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves LE of limousine; LE + P + MI is read backwards. The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push something forward.

clue.text: Spiteful person's nasty brickbat about European leader

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the European leader
something nasty is twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged
a leader is the one in front, so it gives the opening letter of European

explanation.surface: A spiteful person throws a nasty insult at a European leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges BRICKBAT into BACKBITR, which wraps E.
explanation.definitionFit: A backbiter speaks maliciously about people behind their backs, which is spiteful.

clue.text: Independent school administrator available on line, you say?

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after
you say means the word for line is taken by its sound

parts.note: a row is a line
a dean is a college administrator

explanation.surface: Someone mentions an administrator from a private school who can be reached online.
explanation.walkthrough: ROW is spelt ROE when heard. Roedean is a famous girls' boarding school near Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Roedean is a fee-paying girls' school in Sussex, an independent school.

clue.text: Debauched leader capturing western islands

indicators.note: capturing means holding the other piece inside
debauched means corrupted, so the letters are perverted into a new order

explanation.surface: A dissolute leader takes some western islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Debauched' rearranges LEADER into LEEARD, which takes W.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leeward Islands are a Caribbean island group, so the word names islands.

clue.text: Show impressive film set in Dorset's borders

indicators.note: set in means placed inside the other piece
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an epic is a grand, impressive film

explanation.surface: A grand film is being shot on the edges of Dorset, an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' gives D and T from Dorset, the south-west English county.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict something is to show it in a picture or description.

clue.text: Large fish tied to end of the rope

parts.note: a marlin is a large game fish

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A big fish is tied to the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes only the last letter of 'the'; 'end of the rope' tempts you to look at rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Marline is a light two-stranded rope used on ships.

clue.text: Last man in trouble conveyed by small boat

indicators.note: conveyed by means carried inside the other piece

parts.note: a tender is a small boat serving a larger ship
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: The last person is in difficulties, ferried by a dinghy.
explanation.walkthrough: A tail-ender is a cricket term for a weak batsman near the end of the batting order.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a tail-ender bats at the end of the order, often as the last man in.

clue.text: Plaintiff changes direction just once, becoming willing to please

indicators.note: a compass point is swapped for another at a single place in the word for a plaintiff

parts.note: a complainant is the plaintiff in a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A litigant suddenly switches tack and becomes accommodating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes direction just once' swaps one N (north) for S (south); the word has two Ns, only one changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaisant means obliging and keen to do what others want.

clue.text: Chasing wicket, cricket side secured victory

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the side comes after the wicket

parts.note: W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team chasing a total took the vital wicket and won.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Won is the past tense of win, so it means secured victory.

clue.text: Dashed account is out of funds, presumably

indicators.note: an account that is out of funds is in the red, so is here means sits inside

parts.note: being in the red means being overdrawn

explanation.surface: An overdrawn account suggests someone has been rushing to spend.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as AC is (in) RED, the idiom for an overdrawn account; 'presumably' flags that implied 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raced and dashed both mean ran or moved fast.

clue.text: Cruel people uttered Asian tirades

indicators.note: uttered means spoken, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: Thai rants are tirades from Thailand

explanation.surface: Harsh people deliver long angry speeches in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: THAI RANTS said aloud is TYRANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrants are oppressive rulers, people who behave cruelly.

clue.text: You sit around in old pub

indicators.note: around means the second word is wrapped round the first

parts.note: to pose is to sit for a portrait
thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: You are sitting about in an old tavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' says the word for sit is split to hold the old pronoun; 'old' belongs with pub in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothouse is an archaic name for a small, humble pub or alehouse.

clue.text: Last to leave class, I state, unqualified

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for class leaves it

parts.note: a category is a class
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: I report that the last pupil has left the classroom, without question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last to leave' removes Y from CATEGORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A categorical statement is absolute, with no qualification or reservation.

clue.text: Highly valued, I'm engaged by English firm

indicators.note: engaged by means held within, here inside the word for firm

parts.note: stable means firm and steady
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being highly prized and taken on by an English company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company but is the adjective STABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimable means deserving esteem, so it is highly valued.

clue.text: Beds turned over by sleeper, penniless squatter?

indicators.note: turned over means the word for beds is reversed

parts.note: cots are beds

indicators.note: penniless means losing every penny, P, from the word for sleeper

parts.note: a kipper is one who kips, a sleeper

explanation.surface: A homeless squatter turns over beds for a sleeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' makes STOC of COTS; 'penniless' drops both Ps from KIPPER, leaving KIER. The question mark flags squatter as the comparative of squat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockier means more thickset, which is squatter in the comparative sense of squat.

clue.text: After test learner enters gym lesson

indicators.note: after means the first piece comes before what follows

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: enters means goes inside the other piece

parts.note: PE, physical education, is gym class
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: After an exam, a novice turns up for a gym class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gym lesson' looks like one phrase but gym gives PE and lesson is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An example can be a warning or lesson to others, as in making an example of someone.

clue.text: Headgear hatter, I believe, packs up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from bottom to top
packs means holds inside, so the letters are found within the phrase

explanation.surface: A hatmaker gathers up headwear, or so someone supposes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packs' finds ATTERIB in 'hatter, I believe' and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is a square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy, a piece of headgear.

clue.text: Trumped black king during fresh deal

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the king goes inside
fresh means new, so the letters are made over into another order

parts.note: R, from Latin rex, means king

explanation.surface: A card player trumped the black king in a new deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges DEAL to LAED, which takes R. 'Trumped' is not the card sense: it means sounded like a trumpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumped can mean sounded out like a trumpet, which is what blared means.

clue.text: Path with trees watered regularly, absorbing litre after litre

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the selected letters hold the litres
regularly means every other letter is taken
after simply puts one litre next to the other

explanation.surface: A tree-lined path was watered at intervals, soaking up litre after litre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes AEE from watered, and LL goes in after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An allee is a formal avenue or walk lined with trees in a garden.

clue.text: Stop players having day off

indicators.note: off means removed, so the day is taken away

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, players

explanation.surface: The musicians stop for a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' takes D from BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban something is to stop or forbid it.
